metadata.title: How to Detect the Network Status in a Capacitor App
metadata.description: Detect the network status in a Capacitor app: read online/offline state, listen for changes, verify real internet access, and handle metered networks.

faq.question: How do I check if the device is online in Capacitor?
faq.answer: Install @capacitor/network and call Network.getStatus(). It returns connected (boolean) and connectionType ('wifi', 'cellular', 'none' or 'unknown'). Add a networkStatusChange listener to react when the connection changes.

faq.question: Why does Capacitor say I am connected when nothing loads?
faq.answer: connected only means the device has an active network interface. A captive portal, a router without upstream internet, a blocked DNS or a down API all report connected: true. Confirm reachability with a short HTTP request to your own backend, or read internetReachable from @capgo/capacitor-network-diagnostics, which uses Android's validated network capability.

faq.question: Do I need any permission to read the network status?
faq.answer: No runtime permission. On Android the plugins declare ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE in their own manifest, which is a normal install-time permission. iOS needs nothing.

faq.question: Is navigator.onLine enough in a Capacitor app?
faq.answer: It works for a rough signal and fires online and offline events in the WebView, but it cannot tell Wi-Fi from cellular, cannot detect metered or Low Data Mode connections, and is unreliable on some Android WebViews. Use the native plugin on device and keep navigator.onLine as a web fallback.

faq.question: How can I detect a metered or Low Data Mode connection?
faq.answer: Call NetworkDiagnostics.getNetworkStatus() from @capgo/capacitor-network-diagnostics. expensive is true for metered or cellular paths, and constrained is true when iOS Low Data Mode is on. Use these flags to skip large downloads or video autoplay.
